questions.q: If n is even and the middle term in the expansion of $\left(x^2 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)^n$ is $924x^6$, then n is equal to
questions.explanation: Middle term (r = n/2) has exponent of x equal to $2n-3r = n/2$. Setting $n/2 = 6$ gives $n=12$, and $\binom{12}{6}=924$ confirms it.

questions.q: The 13th term in the expansion of $\left(x^2 + \dfrac{2}{x}\right)^n$ is independent of $x$ then the sum of the divisors of $n$ is
questions.explanation: The 13th term has $r=12$: $T_{13}\propto x^{2n-2r-r}=x^{2n-3r}$. Setting $2n-36=0$ gives $n=18$. Divisors of 18 are $1,2,3,6,9,18$, summing to $39$.

questions.q: If $n$ is an odd positive integer and $(1+x+x^2+x^3)^n=\displaystyle\sum_{r=0}^{3n} a_r x^r$, then $a_0-a_1+a_2-a_3+.........-a_{3n}$ is = .................
questions.explanation: Putting $x=-1$ gives the alternating sum $=(1-1+1-1)^n=0^n=0$ since $n\geq 1$.

questions.q: If $r^{th}$ and $(r+1)^{th}$ terms in the expansion of $(p+q)^n$ are equal, then $\dfrac{(n+1)q}{r(p+q)}$ is ..........
questions.explanation: $T_r=T_{r+1}$ gives $\binom{n}{r-1}p^{n-r+1}q^{r-1}=\binom{n}{r}p^{n-r}q^r$, which simplifies to $pr=q(n-r+1)$, i.e. $q(n+1)=r(p+q)$, so the ratio equals 1.
